title: Sort each soil sample into the correct Indian soil type
instructions: Read the description on each card and decide which of India's six major soil types it best belongs to. Use the regions and crops described in the chapter.

bins.name: Alluvial
bins.description: Most widespread; northern plains and deltas; deposited by Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra; very fertile.

bins.name: Black (Regur)
bins.description: Deccan trap on basalt; clayey; great moisture-holding; ideal for cotton.

bins.name: Red and Yellow
bins.description: Crystalline igneous rocks of the Deccan; iron-rich; reddish or yellow when hydrated.

bins.name: Laterite
bins.description: High-temperature, high-rainfall regions; intense leaching; low humus; tea, coffee, cashew.

bins.name: Arid
bins.description: Sandy and saline; western Rajasthan; kankar layer below restricts water.

bins.name: Forest
bins.description: Hilly / mountainous areas with rain forests; loamy in valleys, coarse on slopes.
